required_outcomes: Contacts Keystone Compliance the same day to find out why nobody attended on 8 September and to get a new date as soon as possible, passing on the tenant's availability (weekday afternoons from 2pm, all day Friday).
Replies to the tenant with an apology, saying the agency is chasing the provider and will confirm a new date, without promising one the provider has not given.
Keeps the job on hold for the provider with a follow-up on the next working day, and does not escalate a first missed visit.
acceptable_alternatives: Phoning the provider rather than emailing, as long as the chase and any answer are recorded.
Letting the landlord know about the missed visit and the delay, in addition to chasing the provider.
positive_behaviours: Notices that 8 September was only ever confirmed through the tenant, never by the provider in writing, and asks the provider to confirm the new date in writing to the agency.
Notes the job still shows 30/08/2025 as the visit date and corrects the record.
red_flags: Escalating to a human, or switching to a different contractor, after a single missed visit without first chasing the assigned provider.
Telling the tenant a new date before the provider has confirmed it.
prohibited_actions: Recording a new visit date that the provider has not confirmed.
critical_failures: Leaving the no-show unanswered: no contact with the provider and no reply to the tenant.
